source.title: Relearning Forgotten Knowledge: on Forgetting, Overfit and Training-Free Ensembles of DNNs

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own epoch-wise test-accuracy results bearing on double descent, using image-classification experiments and also introducing a separate forgetting metric.
record.gate_note: The paper reports epoch-wise test-accuracy curves for noisy-label settings and describes the clean-label results in text. Its model-size and training-data comparisons measure forget fraction, not test error; they are recorded as findings that fit no listed version. The accuracy values in the epoch-wise plots are not numerically stated. Ensemble-performance tables and cited results do not test the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The paper reports its own epoch-wise test-accuracy curves on noisy-label CIFAR100 and TinyImagenet (Fig. 1a–b), showing the double ascent. It also reports that test accuracy never decreases in clean-label runs. These results bear on V2 and on the label-noise part of V6. Its model-size and data-size comparisons measure forget fraction, not test error.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Authors conclude that overfit occurs locally as forgetting of test subregions, even when test accuracy keeps rising. In epoch-wise double descent under label noise, the second ascent comes from learning new patterns, mainly from clean data, not relearning forgotten examples. They also propose the KF checkpoint ensemble, which gains about 1% on Imagenet.
record.recipe_differences: Measures test accuracy over training epochs in image-classification experiments and presents curves as accuracy double ascent; it also introduces forget fraction. The paper does not claim to reproduce the original studies.
record.method_sensitivity: The epoch-wise double-descent examples use datasets with 20% symmetric label noise; the paper contrasts these with clean-label benchmark experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Forget fraction increases with ConvNeXt size (small/base/large) on Imagenet, while overall test accuracy barely moves.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Larger models forget more test examples during training even without classical overfit.

fits_no_version.finding: Forget fraction is significantly larger when Resnet18 trains on 10% of CIFAR100 than on larger fractions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Smaller training sets increase test-example forgetting during training.

fits_no_version.finding: During the second accuracy ascent under label noise, newly learned test examples are mostly ones never learned before. Large-loss training examples are mostly clean (Fig. 1c–d).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The second epoch-wise descent reflects learning new patterns from clean data, not relearning forgotten examples.

record.problems: The epoch-wise test-accuracy curves are figure-only and have no stated uncertainty estimates or numerical values. The text does not identify the model architecture for the Figure 1 curves. The reported clean-label summary is not broken out by individual model or dataset.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows extracted from Figure 1c–d: these panels compare clean and noisy training examples with large loss, not the test-error trajectory named by the versions. Ensemble comparison tables report classification accuracy of the proposed method and baselines, not the claim's model-size, epoch-wise, or data-size test-error curves.

untested.parts: No test-error sweep over model size near the interpolation threshold. Table 10 has only three ConvNeXt sizes on Imagenet, far from interpolation.
No test error as a function of sample size.
No effective-complexity predictor of peak location.
Variance as driver, multiple/triple descent, and removal under optimal regularization are not tested.

missing.what: Single-network test accuracy for ConvNeXt small/base/large on Imagenet: 83.21, 83.31, 82.92. This is a model-size vs test-accuracy result, though not near interpolation.
Noisy-label training used cosine annealing with warm restarts every 40 epochs, lr 0.1; this is a condition for r1/r2.

record.verdict_notes: The paper is primarily a methods paper (KF ensemble); its double-descent evidence is qualitative and figure-only. The warm-restart schedule in the noisy runs could contribute to the accuracy dips; researchers should check Fig. 1 dashed-line timing against the 40-epoch restarts. Ensemble tables are the study's own method vs baselines and are correctly excluded.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test test error as model size grows; its model-size comparison measures forget fraction.
The epoch-wise results are described for the tested image-classification settings; the study does not establish the shape across other model classes or settings.
The data-size comparison measures forget fraction, not test error near an interpolation threshold.
No general cross-model-class capacity sweep of risk is reported.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as a predictor of peak location.

The study examines epoch-wise behavior in label-noise settings and describes clean-label behavior, but does not test variance as a driver, multiple or triple descent, or whether optimally tuned regularization removes the peak.
No re-counting of complexity by an effective number of parameters is tested.
